s: austerities has value (visible)
q: 'The value of penance has become visible, birth appears of no value! Look at the holy Harikêsa, the son of a Svapâka, whose power is so great.'

s: merit is produced by benevolence (as the return for gifts)
q: The husbandmen throw the corn on high ground and on low ground, hoping (for a return). For the like motive give unto me; I may be the field which may produce merit (as the return for your benevolence).

s: Law is a pond (for spiritual purification)
q: The Law is my pond, celibacy my holy bathing-place, which is not turbid, and throughout clear for the soul; there I make ablutions; pure, clean, and thoroughly cooled I get rid of hatred (or impurity).

s: sin is caused by injury to living beings (through ignorant ritual practice)
q: You (use) Kusa-grass, sacrificial poles, straw and wood, you touch water in the evening and in the morning; thereby you injure living beings, and in your ignorance you commit sins again and again.

s: Harikêsa-Bala born in Svapâkas (Kândâlas) (a family of)
q: Harikêsa-Bala was born in a family of Svapâkas (Kândâlas); he became a monk and a sage, possessed of the highest virtues, who had subdued his senses.

s: Self-control is a way of life (involving abstention from injury, lying, theft, property, women, pride, and deceit)
q: Doing no injury to living beings of the six orders, abstaining from lying and from taking what is not freely given, renouncing property, women, pride, and deceit, men should live under self-restraint.

s: Karman is a fuel (in Harikêsa-Bala's inner sacrifice)
q: Penance is my fire; life my fireplace; right exertion is my sacrificial ladle; the body the dried cowdung; Karman is my fuel; self-control, right exertion, and tranquillity are the oblations, praised by the sages, which I offer.

s: celibacy is a holy bathing-place (not turbid and clear for the soul)
q: The Law is my pond, celibacy my holy bathing-place, which is not turbid, and throughout clear for the soul; there I make ablutions; pure, clean, and thoroughly cooled I get rid of hatred (or impurity).

s: injury to living beings is avoided by men (to living beings of the six orders)
q: Doing no injury to living beings of the six orders, abstaining from lying and from taking what is not freely given, renouncing property, women, pride, and deceit, men should live under self-restraint.

s: fire is a ritual element (tended by Brahmanas)
q: O Brâhmanas, why do you tend the fire, and seek external purity by water?

s: offerings are Self-control (together with right exertion and tranquillity)
q: Penance is my fire; life my fireplace; right exertion is my sacrificial ladle; the body the dried cowdung; Karman is my fuel; self-control, right exertion, and tranquillity are the oblations, praised by the sages, which I offer.

s: water is used for external purity (in Brahmanical ritual)
q: O Brâhmanas, why do you tend the fire, and seek external purity by water?

s: food and drink is received by Harikêsa-Bala (after a whole-month fast)
q: The noble (monk) said 'yes,' and took food and drink after having fasted a whole month.

s: Harikêsa-Bala observes Samitis (with regard to walking, begging, speaking, easing nature, and receiving and keeping necessities)
q: He observed the rules with regard to walking, begging, speaking, easing nature, and receiving and keeping (of things necessary for a monk) controlled himself, and was always attentive (to his duty).

s: corporal punishment is committed by young men (with sticks, canes, and whips)
q: On these words of the teachers, many young fellows rushed forward, and they all beat the sage with sticks, canes, and whips.

s: rain of perfumed water and flowers is caused by gods (as a response to the gift)
q: At that moment the gods caused a rain of perfumed water and flowers, and showered down heavenly treasures; they struck the drums, and in the air they praised the gift.

s: bathing is a great bath (praised by the seers)
q: The clever ones have discovered such bathing, it is the great bath praised by the seers, in which the great seers bathe, and, pure and clean, they obtain the highest place.

s: bathing purifies soul (through celibacy as the holy bathing-place)
q: The Law is my pond, celibacy my holy bathing-place, which is not turbid, and throughout clear for the soul; there I make ablutions; pure, clean, and thoroughly cooled I get rid of hatred (or impurity).

s: six orders of living beings are protected from injury to living beings (by self-controlled men)
q: Doing no injury to living beings of the six orders, abstaining from lying and from taking what is not freely given, renouncing property, women, pride, and deceit, men should live under self-restraint.

s: Harikêsa-Bala subdues his senses
q: He protected from sin his thoughts, speech, and body, and subdued his senses.

s: Harikêsa-Bala practices asking for something (by begging for food)
q: I am a chaste Sramana, controlling myself; I have no property, nothing belonging to me, and do not cook my food; I have come for food which is dressed for somebody else at the time when I call.

s: Harikêsa-Bala has no property (as a mendicant)
q: I am a chaste Sramana, controlling myself; I have no property, nothing belonging to me, and do not cook my food; I have come for food which is dressed for somebody else at the time when I call.

s: Harikêsa-Bala is protected by Guptis (as a restrained monk)
q: If you do not give me what I ask for, I who observe the Samitis, who am protected by the Guptis, who subdue my senses, what benefit, then, will you gain by your sacrifices?

s: Harikêsa-Bala is attended by The Yakshas
q: There is not the least hatred in me, neither now, nor before, nor in future. The Yakshas attend upon me, therefore they have beaten the boys.

s: Sambhûta is a Kândâla (in a former birth)
q: Being contemptuously treated for the sake of his birth (as a Kândâla) Sambhûta took, in Hastinâpura, the sinful resolution

s: Kitra is born as a merchant (in Purimatâla)
q: Kitra, however, was born in the town Purimatâla in the great family of a merchant

s: Kitra enters the order (after hearing the Law)
q: when he had heard the Law, he entered the order.

s: Kitra is brother of Sambhûta (in a former birth)
q: We were brothers once, kind to each other, loving each other, wishing well to each other.

s: Kitra is a monk (after entering the order)
q: A song of deep meaning condensed in words has been repeated in the midst of a crowd of men, (having heard) which monks of piety and virtues exert themselves in this (religion): I have become a Sramana.

s: Kitra is indifferent to pleasures (as a great sage of excellent conduct and penance)
q: But Kitra the great sage, of excellent conduct and penance, was indifferent to pleasure

s: Kitra reaches the world of perfection (after practising the highest self-control)
q: after he had practised the highest self-control, he reached the highest place of perfection.

s: Brahmadatta is a universal monarch (powerful and glorious king of the Pañkâlas)
q: The universal monarch Brahmadatta, the powerful and glorious king, respectfully addressed the following words

s: Brahmadatta is born of Kulanî (in Kâmpilya)
q: he was born of Kulanî in Kâmpilya as Brahmadatta

s: Brahmadatta is king of the Pañkâlas
q: And Brahmadatta, king of the Pañkâlas, did not act on the counsel of the saint

s: Brahmadatta owns Ukka (a beautiful palace)
q: Renowned are my beautiful palaces Ukka, Udaya, Madhu, Karka, and Brahman

s: Sambhûta takes the sinful resolution (in Hastinâpura, in a former birth)
q: Being contemptuously treated for the sake of his birth (as a Kândâla) Sambhûta took, in Hastinâpura, the sinful resolution (to become a universal monarch in some later birth)

s: Brahmadatta owns Udaya (a beautiful palace)
q: Renowned are my beautiful palaces Ukka, Udaya, Madhu, Karka, and Brahman

s: Brahmadatta owns Madhu (a beautiful palace)
q: Renowned are my beautiful palaces Ukka, Udaya, Madhu, Karka, and Brahman

s: Brahmadatta owns Karka (a beautiful palace)
q: Renowned are my beautiful palaces Ukka, Udaya, Madhu, Karka, and Brahman

s: Brahmadatta owns Brahman (a beautiful palace)
q: Renowned are my beautiful palaces Ukka, Udaya, Madhu, Karka, and Brahman

s: Brahmadatta is attached to pleasures
q: O Kitra, in Hastinâpura I saw the powerful king (Sanatkumâra), and I took that sinful resolution in my desire for sensual pleasures.

s: Brahmadatta does not abandon pleasures (despite knowing the Law)
q: And since I did not repent of it, this has come of it, that I still long for sensual pleasures, though I know the Law.

s: Hastinâpura is where the sinful resolution (is taken by Sambhûta)
q: Sambhûta took, in Hastinâpura, the sinful resolution

s: Kâmpilya is where Brahmadatta (is born)
q: he was born of Kulanî in Kâmpilya as Brahmadatta

s: Kâmpilya is where Sambhûta (and Kitra meet again)
q: In the town Kâmpilya, both Sambhûta and Kitra (as they were called in a former birth) met again

s: the Pañkâlas is king (of the Pañkâlas)
q: And Brahmadatta, king of the Pañkâlas

s: Sambhûta is born as Brahmadatta (in Kâmpilya, after descending from Padmagulma)
q: descending from the heavenly region Padmagulma, he was born of Kulanî in Kâmpilya as Brahmadatta

s: Law is practised by Kitra (as a monk)
q: when he had heard the Law, he entered the order.

s: Law is known by Brahmadatta (despite his continued longing for sensual pleasures)
q: I still long for sensual pleasures, though I know the Law.

s: Karman is produced by sinful thoughts
q: Karman is produced by sinful thoughts

s: Karman follows the doer (and must be borne alone)
q: he alone has to bear it; for the Karman follows the doer.

s: Karman determines a new existence (good or bad)
q: against his will, and accompanied only by his Karman, he enters a new existence, either a good or a bad one.

s: good actions bear fruit (to men)
q: Every good deed will bear its fruit to men

s: good actions produce wealth (as their reward)
q: Know, Sambhûta, that you have got the reward of your virtues in the shape of great wealth and prosperity

s: pleasures produce pains (for the ignorant)
q: pleasures which the ignorant like, but which produce pains

s: pleasures are not permanent transitory
q: the pleasures of men are not permanent

s: Sambhûta is brother of Kitra (in a former birth)
q: We were brothers once, kind to each other, loving each other, wishing well to each other.

s: the order is entered by Kitra (after hearing the Law)
q: when he had heard the Law, he entered the order.

s: the world of perfection is reached by Kitra (after practising the highest self-control)
q: after he had practised the highest self-control, he reached the highest place of perfection.

s: hell is reached by Brahmadatta (after enjoying the highest pleasure)
q: he enjoyed the highest pleasure, and (afterwards) sank into the deepest hell.

s: the sinful resolution is to become a universal monarch (in some later birth)
q: the sinful resolution (to become a universal monarch in some later birth)

s: Sambhûta is separated from Kitra (in the sixth birth)
q: This is our sixth birth, in which we are separated from each other.

s: Sambhûta entertains sinful thoughts (as king)
q: Karman is produced by sinful thoughts, and you have entertained them, O king

s: Sambhûta receives wealth (as the reward of his virtues)
q: Know, Sambhûta, that you have got the reward of your virtues in the shape of great wealth and prosperity

s: Sambhûta longs for pleasures (despite knowing the Law)
q: that I still long for sensual pleasures, though I know the Law.

s: Sambhûta sinks into hell (after enjoying the highest pleasure)
q: And Brahmadatta, king of the Pañkâlas, did not act on the counsel of the saint; he enjoyed the highest pleasure, and (afterwards) sank into the deepest hell.

s: Ishukâra is a town (ancient, wealthy, famous, and beautiful like heaven)
q: some were born (here below) in the ancient, wealthy, and famous town called Ishukâra, which is beautiful like heaven.

s: the two sons of Bhrigu become Sramanas (possessed of many virtues)
q: We shall become Sramanas, possessed of many virtues, and wander about collecting alms.

s: Samsâra is a Wheel of Births
q: hoping to escape the Wheel of Births

s: Samsâra causes fear (fear of worldly existence)
q: Disgusted with the world and afraid of the Samsâra

s: Death harasses the world
q: Mankind is harassed by Death

s: domestic life is rejected by the two sons of Bhrigu (because human life is transitory and short)
q: Seeing that the lot of man is transitory and precarious, and that his life lasts not long, we take no delight in domestic life

s: wandering mendicant life is a life of a monk
q: I shall lead the life of a monk.

s: king Ishukâra is a king
q: the fifth) the widely-famed king Ishukâra

s: pleasures are an obstacle to liberation (bringing slight happiness and prolonged intense suffering)
q: they are an obstacle to the liberation from existence, and are a very mine of evils.

s: pleasures cause worldly existence (continuing worldly existence)
q: pleasures are causes for the continuance of worldly existence

s: liberation is sought by the two sons of Bhrigu
q: Averse to human and heavenly pleasures, desiring liberation

s: Law is adopted by the two sons of Bhrigu (to avoid rebirth)
q: We will even now adopt the Law, after the adoption of which we shall not be born again.

s: Law saves the world (at death, and nothing else does)
q: the Law alone, and nothing else in this world, will save you, O monarch.

s: the soul is eternal (because it possesses no corporeal form)
q: since it possesses no corporeal form it is eternal.

s: the soul is produced in the body (according to the Purôhita's teaching)
q: so, my sons, is the soul produced in the body

s: the soul has bad qualities (these cause its fetter)
q: The fetter of the soul has been ascertained to be caused by its bad qualities

s: worldly existence is caused by the fetter of the soul
q: this fetter is called the cause of worldly existence.

s: the world is consumed by the fire of love and hatred (while beings remain attached to pleasure)
q: the world is consumed by the fire of love and hatred.

s: king Ishukâra has wife Kamalâvatî
q: the fifth) the widely-famed king Ishukâra, and (the sixth) his wife Kamalâvatî

s: the world is disliked by Kamalâvatî (like a bird dislikes a cage)
q: As a bird dislikes the cage, so do I (dislike the world).

s: the two sons of Bhrigu reach perfection (with their parents and the royal couple)
q: The king and the queen, the Brahmanical Purôhita, his wife, and his sons, they all reached perfection.

s: Kamalâvatî is wife of king Ishukâra
q: the fifth) the widely-famed king Ishukâra, and (the sixth) his wife Kamalâvatî

s: Bhrigu became the Purôhita
q: the third became) the Purôhita (Bhrigu)

s: Bhrigu has wife Yasâ
q: the third became) the Purôhita (Bhrigu), (the fourth) his wife Yasâ

s: the two sons of Bhrigu are sons of Bhrigu (both dear sons)
q: Both dear sons of the Brahmanical Purôhita

s: the two sons of Bhrigu are bachelors bachelors (before entering the order)
q: Two males remained bachelors

s: the two sons of Bhrigu seek liberation (averse to human and heavenly pleasures and full of faith)
q: Averse to human and heavenly pleasures, desiring liberation, and full of faith

s: Nirgrantha is a true monk
q: then he is a true monk.

s: Nirgrantha is versed in sacred lore
q: versed in the sacred lore,

s: Nirgrantha protects soul (from every wrong)
q: protecting his soul (from every wrong),

s: Nirgrantha is attached to nothing (not attached)
q: he who is attached to nothing, is a true monk.

s: Nirgrantha endures everything
q: when he endures everything, then he is a true monk.

s: Nirgrantha is content with lowly beds and lodgings
q: He who is content with lowly beds and lodgings,

s: Nirgrantha bears heat and cold
q: bears heat and cold, flies and gnats,

s: Nirgrantha does not expect respectful treatment
q: He does not expect respectful treatment, nor hospitality, nor reverence, nor, indeed, praises;

s: Nirgrantha does not expect hospitality
q: He does not expect respectful treatment, nor hospitality, nor reverence, nor, indeed, praises;

s: Nirgrantha does not expect reverence
q: He does not expect respectful treatment, nor hospitality, nor reverence, nor, indeed, praises;

s: Nirgrantha does not expect praises
q: He does not expect respectful treatment, nor hospitality, nor reverence, nor, indeed, praises;

s: Nirgrantha adopts Law (with the intention to live as a monk)
q: He who adopts the Law in the intention to live as a monk, should live in company (with other monks), upright, and free from desire;

s: Nirgrantha controls himself
q: he controls himself, keeps the vows, practises austerities,

s: Nirgrantha keeps vows
q: he controls himself, keeps the vows, practises austerities,

s: Nirgrantha practises austerities
q: he controls himself, keeps the vows, practises austerities,

s: Nirgrantha meditates on soul (while living together with other monks)
q: lives together with other monks, meditates on his soul;

s: Nirgrantha abandons delusion (every delusion)
q: If he does not care for his life, or abandons every delusion,

s: Nirgrantha avoids men
q: if he avoids men and women,

s: Nirgrantha avoids women
q: if he avoids men and women,

s: Nirgrantha does not practise divination (for livelihood from various signs and omens)
q: He who does not profess and live on divination from cuts and shreds, from sounds on the earth or in the air, from dreams, from diagrams, sticks, and properties of buildings, from changes in the body, from the meaning of the cries (of animals)--he is a true monk.

s: Nirgrantha abstains from medical treatment (including spells, roots, and every kind of treatment)
q: Spells, roots, every kind of medical treatment, emetics, purgatives, fumigation, anointing of the eye, and bathing, the patient's lamentation, and his consolation--he who abstains from all these things, is a true monk.

s: Nirgrantha does not praise warriors
q: He who does not praise, or pay attention to, the warriors, Ugras, princes, Brâhmanas, Bhôgas, and artists of all sorts,

s: Nirgrantha lives in company with fellow-monk
q: should live in company (with other monks)

s: Nirgrantha does not praise Ugras
q: He who does not praise, or pay attention to, the warriors, Ugras, princes, Brâhmanas, Bhôgas, and artists of all sorts,

s: Nirgrantha does not praise princes
q: He who does not praise, or pay attention to, the warriors, Ugras, princes, Brâhmanas, Bhôgas, and artists of all sorts,

s: Nirgrantha does not praise Brâhmanas
q: He who does not praise, or pay attention to, the warriors, Ugras, princes, Brâhmanas, Bhôgas, and artists of all sorts,

s: Nirgrantha does not praise Bhôgas
q: He who does not praise, or pay attention to, the warriors, Ugras, princes, Brâhmanas, Bhôgas, and artists of all sorts,

s: Nirgrantha does not praise artists (of all sorts)
q: He who does not praise, or pay attention to, the warriors, Ugras, princes, Brâhmanas, Bhôgas, and artists of all sorts,

s: Nirgrantha does not improve acquaintance with householders (for earthly gain)
q: He who does not, for earthly gain, improve his acquaintance with householders, with whom he fell in as a monk, or was in friendly relation before that time, he is a true monk.

s: Nirgrantha does not take food and drink (from householders unless they give it themselves)
q: A Nirgrantha is forbidden to take from householders, if they do not give it themselves, bed, lodging, drink, food, or any dainties and spices;

s: Nirgrantha does not take dainties and spices (from householders unless they give them themselves)
q: A Nirgrantha is forbidden to take from householders, if they do not give it themselves, bed, lodging, drink, food, or any dainties and spices;

s: Nirgrantha is not angry such occasions (when householders do not give food, drink, dainties, or spices)
q: he who is not angry at such occasions, he is a true monk.

s: Nirgrantha does not feel compassion for fellow-monk (after receiving food and drink or dainties and spices; in thoughts, words, and deeds)
q: If a monk gets any food and drink, or dainties and spices, and does not feel compassion (on a sick fellow-monk) in thoughts, words, and deeds, (then he is not a true monk);

s: Nirgrantha is free from desire
q: should live in company (with other monks), upright, and free from desire;

s: Nirgrantha has under discipline thoughts, words, and acts (under strict discipline)
q: but if he has his thoughts, words, and acts under strict discipline, then he is a true monk.

s: Nirgrantha does not despise dish-water (as loathsome food and drink)
q: Dish-water, barley-pap, cold sour gruel, water in which barley has been washed: such loathsome food and drink he should not despise,

s: Nirgrantha does not despise barley-pap (as loathsome food and drink)
q: Dish-water, barley-pap, cold sour gruel, water in which barley has been washed: such loathsome food and drink he should not despise,

s: Nirgrantha does not despise cold sour gruel (as loathsome food and drink)
q: Dish-water, barley-pap, cold sour gruel, water in which barley has been washed: such loathsome food and drink he should not despise,

s: Nirgrantha does not despise water in which barley has been washed (as loathsome food and drink)
q: Dish-water, barley-pap, cold sour gruel, water in which barley has been washed: such loathsome food and drink he should not despise,

s: Nirgrantha calls at householders (at the lowliest houses for alms)
q: but call at the lowliest houses (for alms);

s: Nirgrantha does not tremble at voices (dreadful, frightful, and awful noises of gods, men, and beasts)
q: There are many voices on the earth, of gods, of men, and of beasts, dreadful, frightful, and awful noises; if he hears them without trembling, then he is a true monk.

s: voices are spoken by gods (on the earth)
q: There are many voices on the earth, of gods, of men, and of beasts,

s: voices are spoken by men (on the earth)
q: There are many voices on the earth, of gods, of men, and of beasts,

s: Nirgrantha abandons friends (former connections)
q: he should abandon his former connections,

s: Nirgrantha understands religious disputations (all)
q: He who understands all religious disputations, [who lives together with fellow-monks],

s: Nirgrantha practises self-discipline
q: who practises self-discipline, who meditates on his soul,

s: Nirgrantha is calm calm
q: who is calm, and does not hurt anybody,

s: Nirgrantha does not hurt anybody
q: who is calm, and does not hurt anybody,

s: Nirgrantha does not live by any art
q: He who, not living by any art, without house,

s: Nirgrantha is without house
q: without house,

s: Nirgrantha is without friends
q: without friends,

s: Nirgrantha subdues senses (his)
q: subduing his senses,

s: Nirgrantha is free from ties (all)
q: free from all ties,

s: Nirgrantha is sinless sinless
q: sinless,

s: Nirgrantha wanders as unknown beggar (without longing for pleasures)
q: and not longing for pleasures, he should wander about as an unknown beggar:

s: Nirgrantha eats little (but little)
q: and eating but little,

s: Nirgrantha lives single (after leaving the house)
q: leaves the house and lives single,

s: soul is protected by Nirgrantha (from every wrong)
q: protecting his soul (from every wrong),

s: sins are abstained from by Nirgrantha
q: abstaining from sins,

s: austerities are practised by Nirgrantha
q: keeps the vows, practises austerities,

s: householders are not pursued for earthly gain (by improving acquaintance)
q: He who does not, for earthly gain, improve his acquaintance with householders,

s: food and drink are given by householders (only when given themselves)
q: A Nirgrantha is forbidden to take from householders, if they do not give it themselves, bed, lodging, drink, food,

s: Nirgrantha is free from love
q: Free from love he should live,

s: Nirgrantha is a model of righteousness
q: Free from love he should live, a model of righteousness,

s: Nirgrantha abstains from sins
q: abstaining from sins,

s: Sixteenth Lecture is a lecture
q: Sixteenth Lecture.

s: Nirgrantha avoids women (in places for sleep or rest)
q: but a Nirgrantha should not occupy places, for sleep or rest, frequented by women, cattle, or eunuchs.

s: Nirgrantha avoids cattle (in places for sleep or rest)
q: but a Nirgrantha should not occupy places, for sleep or rest, frequented by women, cattle, or eunuchs.

s: Nirgrantha avoids eunuchs (in places for sleep or rest)
q: but a Nirgrantha should not occupy places, for sleep or rest, frequented by women, cattle, or eunuchs.

s: Nirgrantha does not converse with women
q: 2. A Nirgrantha should not converse with women.

s: Nirgrantha does not sit with women (on the same seat)
q: 3. A Nirgrantha should not sit together with women on the same seat.

s: Nirgrantha does not contemplate women (their charms and beauties)
q: 4. A Nirgrantha should not look at, or contemplate, the charms and beauties of women.

s: Nirgrantha does not listen to women (behind a screen, curtain, or wall)
q: 5. A Nirgrantha should not, behind a screen, or curtain, or wall, listen to the screeching or screaming or singing or laughing or giggling or crying of women.

s: Nirgrantha does not recall pleasant things (pleasures and amusements formerly enjoyed with women)

s: Nirgrantha does not eat well-dressed food and drink

s: Nirgrantha does not consume food and drink (to excess)
q: 8. A Nirgrantha should not eat or drink to excess.

s: Nirgrantha does not wear ornaments
q: 9. A Nirgrantha should not wear ornaments.

s: Nirgrantha does not care for sounds, colours, tastes, smells, and feelings (pleasant things)
q: 10. A Nirgrantha should not care for sounds, colours, tastes, smells, and feelings.

s: monk reach a high degree of self-discipline (by hearing and understanding)
q: by hearing and understanding which the monks will reach a high degree of self-discipline, of Samvara, and of contemplation

s: monk reach self-discipline (a high degree)
q: by hearing and understanding which the monks will reach a high degree of self-discipline, of Samvara, and of contemplation

s: monk reach Samvara (a high degree)
q: by hearing and understanding which the monks will reach a high degree of self-discipline, of Samvara, and of contemplation

s: monk reach contemplation (a high degree)
q: by hearing and understanding which the monks will reach a high degree of self-discipline, of Samvara, and of contemplation

s: monk are protected by three Guptis (well protected)
q: will be well protected (by the three Guptis)

s: monk guard senses
q: will guard their senses, guard their chastity

s: monk guard celibacy (their chastity)
q: will guard their senses, guard their chastity

s: monk attend to religious duties (without remissness)
q: and will thus never be remiss (in the attendance on their religious duties).

s: celibacy has conditions ten (for its realisation)
q: Here, indeed, the venerable Sthaviras have declared ten conditions for the realisation of celibacy

s: pleasant things are like Tâlaputa (poison, for a man who seeks after the true Self)
q: these pleasant things, which are hard to leave, are like the poison Tâlaputa, for a man who seeks after the true Self.

s: pleasant things are hard to leave
q: these pleasant things, which are hard to leave, are like the poison Tâlaputa, for a man who seeks after the true Self.

s: monk avoid pleasant things (which are hard to leave)
q: He should, once for all, abandon pleasant things which are hard to leave
